replaceText.old: widened by rev 21 section B to two occurrences in one file (the frozen rejected-key array plus one refusal site per refusal stage)
replaceText.new: pinned by rev 22 section E to exactly one occurrence in one file - the frozen rejected-key array - which both refusal stages read (a refusal site that reads the array adds no literal occurrence)

prohibitedLiteralsCarveOut.pattern: exactly one frozen array literal at module scope, REJECTED_ENV_KEYS = Object.freeze(["PILOT_APPROVAL_RUN_TOKEN"]), whose only member is the key string; the stage-1 check (before the .env load) and the stage-2 check (after it) both READ that same frozen array and the refusal message takes the key NAME from it, so neither refusal site contains the literal. Rev 22 section E corrects the rev 21 count of two: a refusal site that reads the array contributes no literal occurrence.
prohibitedLiteralsCarveOut.rule: The walker permits exactly this one occurrence, in exactly this file, inside exactly this pattern, and fails on a SECOND occurrence anywhere (this file or any other), on the occurrence appearing outside the Object.freeze array-literal initialiser at module scope, on more or fewer than one refusal site per stage, and on any read of the variable's value. Presence is an own-property test on the environment object, never a truthiness or value test, so a set-but-empty value refuses identically. The value is never printed, logged, hashed, digested, length-measured, compared, persisted, receipted, reported, written to any dashboard payload or artefact, or forwarded; only the key name may appear.
prohibitedLiteralsCarveOut.emission: The refusal message is written synchronously to stderr by a direct process.stderr.write call in the refusal path, then the process exits with code 2. Logger.error MUST NOT be used, nor any other logger, reporter, receipt or dashboard path: utils/Logger.js:107 points logFilePath at reports/execution.log and the write path calls fs.promises.mkdir at :142 and fs.promises.appendFile at :145, so a Logger.error call would create or append reports/execution.log and break the no-other-filesystem-access rule before refusal (rev 22 section D).
prohibitedLiteralsCarveOut.refusal: PILOT_CONFIG_REJECTED_ENV_KEY, exit 2, in EVERY falcon.js invocation (pilot and non-pilot), raised from stage 1 if the key is inherited from the process environment and from stage 2 if the .env load introduced it, before any browser or context launch, any dashboard start, any pilot manifest read, any run artefact creation or modification, and any target or provider contact; the stage-2 .env read through the existing configuration path is the only accepted application filesystem access before refusal (rev 21 section B, channel pinned by rev 22 section D).
prohibitedLiteralsCarveOut.scopeNote: Rev 21 section B replaces the rev 20 B1..B7 scope; rev 22 sections D and E pin the emission channel and the one-literal budget. This intentionally converts a previously ignored environment variable into an explicit configuration error in every invocation; the reason code stays PILOT_CONFIG_REJECTED_ENV_KEY for both stages.
inversionTests: neg-token-refusal-stage1-inherited: the key inherited in the process environment is rejected with exit 2 and reason PILOT_CONFIG_REJECTED_ENV_KEY before the .env load
neg-token-refusal-stage2-dotenv: the key absent from the inherited environment but present in .env is rejected identically immediately after the configuration load
neg-token-refusal-empty: the key set to the empty string is rejected identically in both stages
neg-token-refusal-nonpilot-run: a plain non-pilot run (node falcon.js --no-dashboard) with the key present is rejected with exit 2, proving the refusal is not scoped to pilot mode

neg-token-refusal-order: for both stages, the process exit code is exactly 2; NO file write occurs before exit - reports/execution.log is neither created nor appended (assert its absence, or unchanged size and mtime when it pre-exists) and no file under run/ is created or modified; the refusal text appears on stderr and not on stdout; and the rev 21 ordering assertions (refusal precedes browser launch, dashboard start, any pilot manifest read, any run/ write and any target request) still hold on the ordered event log. The case runs with a clean reports/ directory so the no-write assertion is decisive.
neg-token-refusal-silence: the value string appears in no log line, report, receipt, dashboard payload or artefact
neg-token-refusal-no-measure: no hash, digest, length or comparison of the value exists anywhere in the refusal path

neg-token-refusal-carveout: a SECOND occurrence of the literal anywhere - the clearest case being the key string hard-coded into the stage-2 refusal message instead of read from the frozen array - fails AC-084, as does moving the one permitted occurrence out of the frozen array literal or into another file
